note: Action rules by discipline. Rows sourced from checklist/checklist_rules.py keep that row's id in source_rule and are not restated here; hazard rows are defined below. code_ref cites a section number only; requirement text is paraphrased. code_rule_overrides sets the discipline and hazard per checklist row; it is the domain lead's call, not derived.

hazard_rules.title: Set design flood elevation and protect building systems
hazard_rules.why: The lot falls in a mapped flood hazard area, so the lowest floor and the building's mechanical, electrical and plumbing equipment are governed by the flood-resistant construction requirements rather than by the base code alone.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Elevation certificate or a design flood elevation shown on the drawings

hazard_rules.title: Check egress from any below-grade occupied space
hazard_rules.why: Below-grade dwelling and occupied spaces have drowned occupants in NYC when stormwater entered through the only exit. Confirm a second means of egress and that the unit is a legal occupancy.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Egress plan for the below-grade level, and the certificate of occupancy for that use

hazard_rules.title: Check stormwater flooding outside the FEMA map
hazard_rules.why: The lot sits outside a mapped FEMA special flood hazard area but in a stormwater flood-prone area. Extreme rainfall flooding is not covered by the FEMA map, so a site outside the map is not therefore a site without flood risk.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Site drainage design, and the stormwater flood map layer checked with its date

hazard_rules.title: Resolve the E-designation or remediation requirement
hazard_rules.why: The lot carries an E-designation or sits in a state remediation program, so soil, groundwater or vapour conditions must be addressed before a permit is issued and before occupancy.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: OER or DEC sign-off, remedial action work plan, and the site management plan

hazard_rules.title: Plan excavated soil handling and worker protection
hazard_rules.why: Excavation on a lot with a known contamination history generates regulated soil and exposes workers and neighbours to vapour and dust.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Soil disposal manifests and the community air monitoring plan

hazard_rules.title: Check the facade inspection cycle and any open report
hazard_rules.why: Buildings over six storeys report on their facade condition on a recurring cycle. An overdue or unsafe-filed report on this building or an adjacent one is a falling-object hazard over the sidewalk and a sign of deferred maintenance.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: The most recent filed facade report and its status

hazard_rules.title: Provide pedestrian protection before work at height
hazard_rules.why: Work on or above the building line requires protection of the sidewalk and adjacent public way before that work begins, not after a piece has fallen.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Sidewalk shed or fence permit and an installation record

hazard_rules.title: Maintain means of egress during construction
hazard_rules.why: Alteration work in an occupied building can block or reduce the exits the occupants depend on. Egress has to be maintained throughout the work, not restored at the end.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Site safety plan showing egress maintained at each phase

hazard_rules.title: Verify self-closing doors on dwelling unit entrances
hazard_rules.why: Smoke spread through a multi-unit building has killed occupants in NYC when apartment entrance and stair doors failed to self-close. Any altered or replaced door assembly in this scope has to keep that function.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Door schedule showing self-closing hardware, and an installation inspection

hazard_rules.title: Confirm every gas line alteration is permitted and tested
hazard_rules.why: Unpermitted gas work has destroyed buildings and killed occupants in NYC. Any gas piping touched in this scope needs a permit, a pressure test and a utility sign-off before service is restored.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Gas work permit, pressure test record and utility authorisation

hazard_rules.title: Set a rain and freeze-thaw hold point for the open excavation
hazard_rules.why: Heavy rain and freeze-thaw cycling change the loads on an excavation support system and on adjoining foundations while the cut is open. Decide the thresholds before the cut is open rather than during a storm.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Written hold-point criteria in the monitoring plan, with the rainfall and temperature thresholds

hazard_rules.title: Protect exposed adjoining walls over the winter
hazard_rules.why: A party wall exposed by demolition and left through a winter takes freeze-thaw damage that was not in its original design.
hazard_rules.proof_needed: Weather protection detail and the date it was installed

model_rules_note: Rules that turn a confirmed structural model (a drawing reading the uploader confirmed, or a Revit export) into checklist items for the roles it concerns: actions/from_model.py. A rule with item_id flags that checklist row when the project already has it, instead of adding a second copy. Wording to be confirmed by the domain lead.

model_rules.title: Underpin or support the adjoining buildings
model_rules.why: Where underpinning or another method of support is required, provide it at the builder's expense. The confirmed drawing shows bearing walls on the lot line, so the buildings next door may rest on or against them.
model_rules.proof_needed: Underpinning or support drawings, and records that they were followed

model_rules.title: Notify the adjoining owner
model_rules.why: Written notice to the adjoining owner at least 60 days before work: the work, schedule, inspections or monitoring, protection, and a contact. The confirmed drawing shows bearing walls on the lot line, so the work reaches the neighbour's side.
model_rules.proof_needed: The notice letters and their dates

model_rules.title: Check the bearing walls on the lot line
model_rules.why: The confirmed drawing shows load-bearing walls on the property line. Establish whether each is shared with the building next door and what it carries before excavating beside it or changing its load.
model_rules.proof_needed: Dated examination record of each lot-line wall

model_rules.title: Examine the adjoining building
model_rules.why: Once access is granted, physically examine the adjoining property before work and at intervals during it, record the conditions, and make the records available to DOB. Include the lot-line walls the confirmed drawing shows.

model_rules.title: Check the unreinforced masonry before cutting or loading it
model_rules.why: The confirmed drawing gives the structure as unreinforced masonry. Openings, new loads and vibration near these walls need the engineer's check first.
model_rules.proof_needed: The engineer's check of the affected walls

model_rules.title: Establish the lateral system
model_rules.why: The confirmed drawing does not show what resists wind and seismic load. Establish it before removing or altering walls, floors or bracing.
model_rules.proof_needed: The lateral system shown on the structural drawings or in a field report

model_rules.title: Confirm the existing foundation
model_rules.why: The confirmed drawing does not show the foundation. Confirm its type and depth before digging beside it or adding load.
model_rules.proof_needed: Test pits, probes or record drawings showing the foundation

geotech_rules_note: Rules that turn a confirmed geotechnical report reading into checklist items: actions/from_model.py (geotech_actions). Thresholds (15 ft groundwater, 3 tsf bearing, 20 ft rock) are a first draft for the domain lead to confirm.

geotech_rules.title: Geotechnical basis for the support design
geotech_rules.why: The support drawings rest on site-specific testing, and incorporate the geotechnical report, the evaluation analysis and the preconstruction survey. The confirmed report is that basis.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: The geotechnical report, cross-referenced in the drawings

geotech_rules.title: Plan dewatering for the excavation
geotech_rules.why: The confirmed report found groundwater within 15 ft of grade, near or above the cellar excavation. Pumping it down can settle the neighbours' footings, so the dewatering plan needs the engineer's review before digging.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Dewatering plan reviewed by the engineer

geotech_rules.title: Monitor nearby buildings
geotech_rules.why: Monitor adjoining buildings for movement during excavation and dewatering. The confirmed report found groundwater within 15 ft of grade.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Monitoring readings with dates and thresholds

geotech_rules.title: Waterproof the cellar below the water table
geotech_rules.why: The confirmed report found groundwater within 15 ft of grade, so the new cellar may sit at or below it. Detail waterproofing for water pressure, not only damp-proofing.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Waterproofing details on the architectural drawings

geotech_rules.title: Check the footings against the reported bearing capacity
geotech_rules.why: The confirmed report recommends an allowable bearing pressure below 3 tsf. Check existing and new footings, and the underpinning, against it.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Footing calculations using the reported bearing pressure

geotech_rules.title: Account for fill or soft soil in the support design
geotech_rules.why: The confirmed report found fill or soft soil near the surface. It moves more under load and when dug beside; the support of excavation and underpinning design should account for it.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Support design calculations citing the soil profile

geotech_rules.title: Plan rock removal with vibration limits
geotech_rules.why: The confirmed report found bedrock within 20 ft of grade. Removing it shakes the adjoining buildings; set vibration limits and monitoring before work.
geotech_rules.proof_needed: Rock removal plan with vibration limits
